verses.sanskrit:
डुण्डुभ उवाच।
              सखा बभूव मे पूर्वं खगमो नाम वै द्विजः। भृशं संशितवाक्तात तपोबलसमन्वितः॥१॥
verses.english: The Dundubha said : In time gone by, I had a friend, a Brahmana, by name Khagama. He was truthful and possessed spiritual powers by penances.

verses.sanskrit: स मया क्रीडता बाल्ये कृत्वा तार्णं भुजंगमम्। अग्निहोत्रे प्रसक्तस्तु भीषितः प्रमुमोह वै॥२॥
verses.english: When he was engaged in Agnihotra, out of boyish frivolity, I made a snake of the blades of grass and tried to frighten him. He fainted away (when he saw this mock snake).
verses.bhavadeepa: एकदशः अध्यायः  नर्मपूर्विकाऽपि परपीडा न कर्तव्या किमुत चास्तवी साप्यधर्मेणेत्याहाध्यायेन। सखा बभूवेत्यादिना। खगमो नाम वाडव इति पाठे। वाडवः ब्राह्मणः। संशितवाक् तीक्ष्णवचनः॥१॥

verses.sanskrit: लब्ध्वा स च पुनः संज्ञां मामुवाच तपोधनः। नर्दहन्निव कोपेन सत्यवाक्संशितव्रतः॥३॥
verses.english: Recovering his senses, that truthful and penance-performing Rishi exclaimed to me in anger.

verses.sanskrit: यथा वीर्यस्त्वया सर्पः कृतोऽयं मद्बिभीषया। तथा वीर्यो भुजंगस्त्वं मम शापाद्भविष्यसि॥४॥
verses.english: "As you made a powerful mock snake to frighten me, you will yourself turn into a venomless serpent by my curse."

verses.sanskrit: तस्याहं तपसो वीर्यं जानन्नासं तपोधन। भृशमुद्विग्नहृदयस्तमवोचमहं तदा॥५॥
verses.english: O Rishi, I was well aware of the power of penances that he possessed. Therefore, with an agitated heart, I addressed him thus,

verses.sanskrit: प्रणतः संभ्रमादेव प्राञ्जलिः पुरतः स्थितः। सखेति हसतेदं ते नर्मार्थं वै कृतं मया॥६॥
verses.english: Bending low and joining both hands, "As I am your friend, I have done this only as a joke to make you laugh.

verses.sanskrit: क्षन्तुमर्हसि मे ब्रह्मञ्शापोऽयं विनिवर्त्यताम्। सोऽथ मामब्रवीद्दृष्ट्वा भृशमुद्विग्नचेतसम्॥७॥
verses.english: You should, O Brahmana, pardon me and revoke your curse." Seeing me very much distressed, the ascetic moved and breathing hot and hard, he said, What I have said must happen.
verses.bhavadeepa: संभ्रमात् भयात्। पुर इत्यपेक्षिते पुरत इत्यार्षम्॥६॥

verses.sanskrit: मुहुरुष्णं विनिःश्वस्य सुसंभ्रान्तस्तपोधनः। नानृतं वै मया प्रोक्तं भवितेदं कथंचन॥८॥
यत्तु वक्ष्यामि ते वाक्यं शृणु तन्मे तपोधन। श्रुत्वा च हृदि ते वाक्यमिदमस्तु सदाऽनघ॥९॥
verses.english: O ascetic, listen to what I say and hearing it, O pious man, always keep it to your heart.

verses.sanskrit: उत्पत्स्यति रुरुर्नाम प्रमतेरात्मजः शुचिः। तं दृष्ट्वा शापमोक्षस्ते भविता नचिरादिव॥१०॥
verses.english: When Ruru the holy, the son of Pramati will appear, you will be immediately relieved of the curse on seeing him.”

verses.sanskrit: स त्वं रुरुरितिख्यातः प्रमतेरात्मजोऽपि च। स्वरूपं प्रतिपद्याहमद्य वक्ष्यामि ते हितम्॥११॥
verses.english: You are the very Ruru, the son of Pramati. Now regaining my natural form I shall speak something for your benefit.

verses.sanskrit: स डौण्डुभं परित्यज्य रूपं विप्रर्षभस्तदा। स्वरूपं भास्वरं भूयः प्रतिपेदे महायशाः॥१२॥
verses.english: was Souti said : That illustrious man and the best of Brahmanas then left his snake-body and attained his own form with original brightness.

verses.sanskrit: इदं चोवाच वचनं रुरुमप्रतिमौजसम्। अहिंसा परमो धर्मः सर्वप्राणभृतां वर॥१३॥
verses.english: He then addressed Ruru of incomparable power, saying, “O best of beings, the highest morality is not to hurt others.

verses.sanskrit: तस्मात्प्राणभृतः सर्वान्न हिंस्याद्ब्राह्मणः क्वचित्। ब्राह्मणः सौम्य एवेह भवतीति परा श्रुतिः॥१४॥
verses.english: Therefore, a Brahmana should never hurt any creature. The injunction of the Shruti is that a Brahmana should always be mild.

verses.sanskrit: वेदवेदाङ्गविन्नाम सर्वभूताभयप्रदः। अहिंसा सत्यवचनं क्षमा चेति विनिश्चितम्॥१५॥
verses.english: Learned in the Vedas and the Vedangas and an inspirer of confidence in all creatures, kind to all, truthful and forgiving.

verses.sanskrit: ब्राह्मणस्य परो धर्मो वेदानां धारणापि च। क्षत्रियस्य हि यो धर्मः स हि नेष्येत वै तव॥१६॥
verses.english: And a great retainer of the Vedas in memory, these are the natural duties of a Brahmana. The natural duties of Kshatriya are not those of yours.

verses.sanskrit: दण्डधारणमुग्रत्वं प्रजानां परिपालनम्। तदिदं क्षत्रियस्यासीत्कर्म वै शृणु मे रुरो॥१७॥
verses.english: To be stern, to hold a rod (for punishable), to rule the subjects, are the natural duties of the Kshatriya. Listen to ine, O Ruru.

verses.sanskrit: जनमेजयस्य यज्ञेऽस्मिन्सर्पाणां हिंसनं पुरा। परित्राणं च भीतानां सर्पाणां ब्राह्मणादपि॥१८॥
verses.english: In days of yore, the snakes were destroyed in the sacrifice of Janamejaya, but the terrified snakes were saved by a Brahmana.
It was by Astika learned in the Vedas and the Vedangas and mighty in spiritual power.
verses.bhavadeepa: परित्राणं दृष्टमितिशेषः। परैः हिंस्यमानस्य ब्राह्मणेन कर्तव्यं न तु हिंसेत्यर्थः॥१८॥
